findings.claim: `_batch` passes `stamp_orphaned=True` on the strength of `_resolve_queue`'s documented premise that 'one batch runs at a time,' but nothing in this diff enforces that premise — no lock file, no PID check, nothing like the `flock` the repo already uses elsewhere (`saffron/report/index.py`) when concurrent writers are a real risk. A candidate's own wall-clock ceiling is per-attempt, not per-batch, so a long-running last task can carry the whole night past `--until`; if a second invocation (a retried launchd job, an operator running it by hand, a misconfigured schedule) starts while the first is still mid-candidate, its `_resolve_queue(stamp_orphaned=True)` will stamp the first batch's genuinely in-flight task `ORPHANED` and requeue it, corrupting the ledger in a way the single-process test suite can never exercise.

`_mirror_path` is a third, now-factored-out copy of the digest formula `_resolve_queue` (line 661) and `_run_cell` (line 377) already compute inline, and the docstring's whole point is that `_batch`'s readiness check must probe 'this run's own mirror' — i.e. the same path `_resolve_queue` already resolved. But `test_the_night_is_given_a_real_readiness_check_not_the_loops_default` asserts `seen["mirror_path"] == cli._mirror_path(repo.resolve(), home)`, computing its expected value by calling the very function under test a second time rather than deriving it from `resolved.mirror` (the mirror `_resolve_queue` actually fetched). Slicing the digest to `[:10]` instead of `[:12]` here would make `_batch`'s readiness probe a different, unrelated mirror path than the one the rest of the run uses — exactly the kind of silent landmine the notes warn about — yet the test would stay green because both sides of its assertion recompute with the same (now-divergent) function.
